To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
LPS-induced EGFR signaling in hepatocarcinomas is regulated through HPS70-induced expression of COX2 and that this signaling can be inhibited by TLR4 shRNAs and COX-2 inhibitors.
LPS-induced EGFR phosphorylation involves a bypass feedback loop that involves HSP70 and COX-2.

LPS-induced EGFR phosphorylation involves HSP70-induced COX2 in hepatocarcinomic H22 cells, and inhibition of TLR-4 expression and COX-2 activity could be an effective therapeutic approach for the treatment of hepatocarcinomas.

the role of LPS-induced HSP70/EGFR/COX- 2 signaling in tumor growth and the possibility             that this signaling may provide a novel target for cancer therapy.
